toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The departures are concentrated in the Kestrel team: 8 of the 11 associates on it have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who were never on it. The rest of the firm is at normal attrition levels, so ordinary market movement doesn't explain this. The pay story is weak. Group salaries sit at the same percentile as the rest of the firm. The rival firm pays £3–5k more, not £15k. Most leavers took equal or lower pay. The firm-wide hours target applies everywhere and doesn't explain why one group is affected.

I can't yet separate the two remaining explanations: Kestrel's workload, or Dorian Faulk's supervision. Every Kestrel associate reports to Faulk, and he supervises no one else, so the two always occur together. The survey points to both: unsustainable workload and disrespectful late-night corrections.

I'm fairly sure the problem is Kestrel-specific. I'm not sure which factor is driving it. Don't announce the £12k payment or close the review. Instead, commission the confidential interviews (about £9k, three weeks), designed to separate workload from supervision. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Prepare to change supervision or staffing once the interviews show which factor matters. The document-review phase runs to December, so there is limited time.
